slots.title: Learn mahjong: hub hero
where: /games/mahjong/learn → components/games/mahjong/learn/learn-hub.tsx, the art panel right of the welcome and progress at the top of the page
slots.css: measured: desktop 1440/1280/1021 542×279 (right column of the hub's top block), cover; tablets 721–1020px full content width above the welcome, about 766×332 at 800 wide; phones 341×147 at 375 wide
slots.crop: Composited, not cropped: the figure is scaled so its face lands at a set height and its cut line meets the table edge, and it stands at the frame's right. The frame's measured sizes are in css; tiles fill the room to the figure's left.
slots.lighting: even, flat studio light on a solid backdrop (the composite adds the blue glow)
slots.fallback: Drawn in learn-art.tsx (HubArt): a winning hand of real tiles standing in its five groups on a blue felt rail, the groups lifting one after another, a rising price line behind and three loose tiles drifting above, on a blue halftone wash. Once the talent art ships, the composite replaces it: code background, the talent cutout, the table edge and the real tiles in front.
slots.brief: Gawr Gura, teaching at the board. Waist-up, facing the viewer, in the approved house style (cel shading, clean lineart).
slots.notes: Only the talent is generated: a waist-up cutout in the talent's official outfit on a flat backdrop, with the whole head inside the picture and both arms inside the frame. No mahjong tiles, table, cards, text or letters in the image: the page draws the background glow, the table edge and the game's own tiles (components/games/mahjong/talent-scene.tsx), so every tile face is exact. The manifest entry needs anchors face_y (face center) and cut_y (where the table edge goes), both fractions of the height, and span (the figure's width as a fraction of the image width); without them, or at another size, the drawn version stays.
